note: The ground BETWEEN the stations, gap by gap: what is open, what the book says lies there, what Renaissance practice would put there where the book is silent, the view sequence to protect, and what it costs. Written 2026-09-20 in answer to Ted's live test ('I don't want a bunch of mostly empty spaces between our buildings'). Prose and reasoning: RETHINK.md. Subordinate to research/coverage.json, which remains the ledger of what the book has and the world does not; nothing here promotes a feature's status. Every element carries a `provenance`: `book` (cited to a 1499 page), `ours, after <named precedent>` (a precedent contemporary with or earlier than 1499, or a classical source the humanists read), or `ours, unsupported`.

frame.compass: +z SOUTH, -z NORTH, +x EAST, -x WEST (declared at src/scenes/world/constants.js:34)
frame.note_on_spans: The plan separates consecutive precincts by exactly ONE STADIUM (185 m) almost everywhere, and by two at polia_garden->three_doors. The `open_span_z_m` column is precinct BOX edge to BOX edge, from src/scenes/world/plan_sites.js zSouth/zNorth. The boxes for precincts marked `sized: ours` are plan allocations, not built extents: the geometry actually inside them is authored in stage-1 (x4) coordinates and is in most cases far smaller than its box. So `open_span_z_m` is a LOWER BOUND on the open ground, and the true figure at the Temple of Venus, the Polyandrion and Vertumnus is substantially larger. This was not measured live (see RETHINK.md 'Where this plan is thin').

budget.rule: ENGINEERING.md / CLAUDE.md rule 7. The gate is regression, not an absolute.
budget.world_triangles_cap: +15 % over the hpDiag world-total measured at the START of the first infill ticket. That number is not in this file because no live reading was taken this pass; the first builder records it in the commit message before touching anything.
budget.per_view_cap: No single view's draw calls may rise more than 25 % (rule 7).
budget.why_per_view_matters_more: DRAWCALLS.md: cost is a property of the VIEW, not of the world. None of these eight gaps is ever in the same frustum as the pyramid's north face or as Cythera, so the worst frame in the world (the dark wood, 3 124 calls / 2.92 M tris on 2026-09-09) is untouched by every proposal here.
budget.method: Every proposal is costed on the _isleGrove model (src/scenes/world/cythera.js:840): one InstancedMesh for trunks and one for crowns per species, so a species of any count is TWO draw calls. A tree is ~100 triangles (6-sided trunk cylinder ~36, 7x5 crown sphere ~70, or a 7-sided cone ~14). Hedges are merged box runs, ~12 triangles per 5 m segment. Water is a ribbon plane.

book.words: to this excellent colonnade let its two hundred columns yield - Numidian, Claudian, Simiadic and Thistian, divided in equal number ... What gate-house, or vestibule; what royal portico ... the marvellous ceiling, most beautifully coffered, with little coffers between the wavings, covered with foliage, set in square and round. Adorned with exquisite lineaments, gilded of pure gold and of a dark blue colouring

the way in was closed by a joyful and marvellous curtain stretched across, all of golden thread ... This chief and first curtain it is granted to no one to enter without the receiving of a plain and watchful damsel doorkeeper, called Cynosia ... Here was an enclosed space, divided by another veiling ... a woman likewise careful came immediately to us, named Indalomena
a third matron, our hostess ... Whose name was Mnemosyne ... I saw a lofty portico, as long as the compass of the palace

proposals.element: The palace front as a 200-column colonnade closing the enclosure's north side
proposals.note: Four marbles in equal number, 50 columns each. 200 columns cannot stand in one 88.8 m run at any believable intercolumniation, so the book's 200 is the whole peristyle: the front run closing the enclosure plus the two returns and the inner court. Build the front run and declare the rest.

proposals.note: Answers NEXTSTEPS 0-AA's 'the roof is too low': the existing Queen's Court colonnade is 4.0 m. A two-storey front at ~11 m to the upper cornice reads as monumental against an 88.8 m room.

book.words: we came most festively to a most charming river. Upon the banks of which I saw a gracious plane-grove, besides other greenest little trees, and water shoots excellently set and placed, with lotuses set between. Where there crossed a proud stone bridge of three arches, with its ends upon the banks above the firmest foundations, with the piers keeled at their two fronts to hold the structure most firm, and with most noble parapets

at the middle curve of the wedge beneath the arch, here and there, there stood out, raised and well polished, a porphyry square with a gable, holding a sunk carving of hieroglyphs. On the right at our crossing I saw a matron bound with a serpent, sitting upon one haunch only ... she held a pair of wings, and in the other ... a tortoise. Opposite there was a circle, the centre of which two little spirits held

Which bridge was then of a moderate slope ... Which was all of most comely Hymettian marble. Having passed the bridge, we walked beneath through the cool shades, sweetly kept by the various chattering of small birds. We came to a stony and rocky place, where lofty and steep mountains rose up. And thence next to a broken and pathless and rugged mountain, all gnawed away and full of a bursting roughness. High into the air, worn down to a spur, and bare of all greenness, and dry mountains round about.

these hieroglyphs ... are much to the purpose for one who goes to the three doors. And therefore they are most fitly set here as a monument for those passing by. The circle says: the blessed have held to the middle. The other: temper swiftness by sitting, and slowness by rising.

book.words: the lovely damsels, without my noticing, left me alone, so kindled, in a most pleasant plain ... raising my eyes a little, behold, before me I see only an artful arbour of flowering jasmine, with a tall arching, painted all over with its fragrant little flowers of the three colours mingled. Entering beneath this ...

without noticing, I came to the end of that flowery covering; and looking, there appeared to me a countless crowd of youth of both kinds keeping high festival, with sounding voices and with the melodies of various instruments, with comely and playful dancings and clappings ... solacing themselves in troops upon a most ample plain. So that, seized by this such and welcome novelty, sitting down full of wonder, I stood in thought about going any further.
book.reading: THE STRUCTURE IS EXPLICIT: a covered walk that shows nothing, ended by a reveal that stops him where he stands. This is the single clearest statement in the book of DIRECTIONS.md 5, and it is 185 m long in our plan, which is exactly right for it.

book.words: she led me towards a spacious shore. Which bordered upon the flower-bearing and hilly valley, where the adorned little mountains ended at this shore, and the vine-bearing hills, with their ways shut, enclosing round about this golden country, full of incredible delight. Which were of wooded groves of a notable thickness, as though the little trees had been pleasantly set in order: the yew of Corsica and of Arcady, the fruitless and resinous wild pine, tall pines, straight firs ... the burnable spruce, the spongy larch, airy torch-pines

among the loftiest cypress, among the spreading beeches, among the fruitful and green oaks ... and hard oaks with rough bark, and the pricking junipers that love eternity, and brittle hazels, and the ash for spear-shafts, and the berried laurel, and shady holm-oaks, and knotty hornbeams, and lime trees ... All which trees were not of a thick planting, but dispensed at the required distance, and all duly distributed in a fitting place and aspect

We entered, then, where there were measured square spaces hedged about with the bounds of wide, straight, four-way roads, a pace high, of dog-thorn, or thorny grape, and of ground juniper, and most thickly bound to a wall-like level of most even box, enclosing the squares of the flowering and dewy meadows. In the order of the said hedges I beheld planted symmetrically the lofty victorious palms, with their fruitful clusters of dates hanging out of their sheaths ... Which stood alternating with the greenest citrons and oranges, hawthorn-medlars, pistachios, pomegranates, quinces, tree-myrtles, and medlars, and service-trees, and many other noble fruit trees
book.reading: A hedge one PACE high (1.48 m, a stated measure), clipped to a wall-like level, of box with dog-thorn and ground juniper; square compartments of flowering meadow; wide straight four-way roads; palms planted symmetrically alternating with citrus and fruit trees. This is a specification, not an impression.

proposals.element: The quincunx orchard: a 4 x 4 grid of square compartments across the gap, box hedges 1.48 m high, four-way roads between

proposals.note: Proposed module: compartments of one quarter stadium (46.25 m) square, roads of 5 paces (7.4 m). Both numbers are arithmetic on the book's own units and are marked `ours`. Alberti IX.4 puts villa trees 'in rank and file, answering one another with equal intervals' and walks between compartments; Pliny Ep. V.6 gives the box-bounded compartments the humanists actually pictured. Do NOT cite Villa d'Este or Boboli - both are half a century or more after 1499.

approaches.reason: Chapter II-III is the book's one long approach and it depends on emptiness: 'casting my eyes towards the wooddie mountaines, which seemed to ioyne themselues together, beeing looked vnto a farre off ... the forme of a tower of an incredible heygth, with a spyre vnperfectlie appearing', then 'by how much the more I approximated the same, by so much the more the excellencie of the woorke shewed it selfe' (DIRECTIONS.md 3, rows 7-8; Dall. pp. 25-27). Filling this gap would destroy the one piece of spectacle the world already has the room for.
what_it_does_need: The cliffs must CONVERGE toward the porch so the valley reads as closing - the book's 'no man could go further forward or backe againe'.

Two or three mid-ground scale markers (a milestone, a single tree, the palm) so the pyramid's growth is measurable rather than merely asserted. Provenance: ours, after Alberti IX on the approach that measures itself.
bug-fields-dark-wedge's resolution notes that the valley mountain mass passes within 2.4 m of the old fields station: check that no mass stands in the sightline.

approaches.verdict: INTENTIONAL. Build nothing on the water.
approaches.reason: The crossing fills a whole chapter of song (ch. XX, our pp. 283-289) and its content is the singing, the standard, and Cupid at the prow. DIRECTIONS.md 3, row 24: 'No distance given - but the duration is the fact.'
what_it_does_need: The nymphs' six-part song staged as an event with a duration, not a caption.
Cythera resolving from one mass into three rings over the crossing - an aerial-perspective and LOD question, not new geometry.

reading_faults.title: _buildTrees is never placed, so the garden trees stand inside the pyramid
reading_faults.evidence: src/scenes/HPWorldScene.js:393 calls this._buildTrees() OUTSIDE every _in(...) / _placeAt group. Its coordinates (src/scenes/world/nature.js:988-1018) are the original cramped ones: the myrtle-and-laurel grove of the Fountain of Venus at (0, -20) r 11.5, the cypress pair 'the way to the palace' at z 15.5-24.5, the citron/orange/lemon enclosure at x +/-9 and +/-13.5, planes, oaks and olives out to x +/-29. With no shift those are WORLD coordinates, and the pyramid precinct spans z +104 to -1035.6 centred on x 0. So the Temple of Venus's grove and the green enclosure's citrus hedge are standing in the Great Portal's court and inside the pyramid's own footprint, between 2.7 and 5.3 km from the precincts they belong to.

reading_faults.title: The processional path runs dead straight at x = 0 while three of the last four precincts are 150-430 m off it
reading_faults.evidence: src/scenes/world/approach.js:_buildGround lays ONE 3.4 m path plane the whole length of the plan at x = 0. PLAN_SITES puts vertumnus at x +150, venus_temple at x -200, polyandrion at x +230. The walker therefore steps off the path onto raw ground for the last four stations, and the dog-legs are 350 m and 430 m across nothing.

reading_faults.title: The three-arch bridge of p. 133 is built in the venus_temple precinct
reading_faults.evidence: _buildSecondBridge (src/scenes/world/portal.js:1635) is called at HPWorldScene.js:363 inside _in('venus_temple', ...). Its carved devices - the matron with wings and tortoise, the circle held by two spirits - are the ones Logistica glosses on p. 134 as 'much to the purpose for one who goes to the three doors'. It is about 1 800 m north of where the book sets it.

reading_faults.title: The meadow's blade density fell fourfold at stage 2, so the gardens render as painted lawn
reading_faults.evidence: src/scenes/world/nature.js:_buildMeadow. GARDENS bounds are x -320..320 (640 m) by z -2885.6..-5797.9 (2 912.3 m) = 1 863 872 m2. Desktop counts: grass 36 000 x DENSE 4.0 = 144 000; understorey 22 000 x 4.0 = 88 000; wildflowers 1 000 x 4.0 = 4 000. That is 0.077 grass blades per square metre - ONE BLADE PER 12.8 m2. The comment says the count rises with the bounds, and it did, by 4x; the area rose by 16.3x (the old box was 336 x 340 = 114 240 m2 at 0.315 blades/m2). This is the most likely single cause of 'a wholly empty green field' in Ted's screenshot, and no amount of infill fixes it.

reading_faults.title: The jasmine arbour is in the palace precinct; chapter XI puts it after the third door
reading_faults.evidence: _buildJasmineArbour (src/scenes/world/palace.js:1518) is called inside _in('polia_garden'/'palace'). Our pp. 141-142 put the arbour on the plain where the bath-nymphs leave him, AFTER the doors, and make it the covering he walks under until the festival plain appears. Moving it is also the cheapest way to fill G4.

reading_faults.title: The screenshot's stated bearing does not agree with the declared compass
reading_faults.evidence: NEXTSTEPS 0-AA records 'From the palace precinct (x76, z-3460) looking north, the pyramid and its flanking cliffs stand as a thin sliver on the horizon.' The compass declared at src/scenes/world/constants.js:34 makes -z north, and the pyramid is at z -465.8 while the palace is at -3113.2 - so the pyramid is 2.6 km SOUTH of the camera. Either the camera was facing south, or the label is loose. It does not change the finding (an empty field between camera and horizon) but it changes WHICH gap the finding is about, and nobody should plan off it until it is re-shot.

serialization_note: Every ticket that adds geometry must also add one call in src/scenes/HPWorldScene.js inside the right _in(...) group. That file is the serialization point for the whole programme: one writer at a time, and the infill builders live in a NEW module src/scenes/world/infill.js precisely so that palace.js, temple.js and cythera.js stay free for the builders already working them.
